brief.headline: Cut ₹28.69 L off our annual bill by matching the prices Mars Plastics and Premier Plastic already give us, and tighten payment to 30 days to free ₹16.02 L cash.

priceAsk.summary: Match the prices Mars Plastics and Premier Plastic charge us on the three biggest items.
priceAsk.target: Save ₹28.69 L per year by closing the gap on PP caps (₹1.08 → ₹0.81), HDPE bottles (₹1.53 → ₹1.38), and measuring cups (₹0.46 → ₹0.35).
priceAsk.basis: We already pay ₹0.81/NOS to Mars Plastics for the same PP cap that Cincorp charges ₹1.08 — a 33.2% gap. Same story on bottles (10.7% gap) and cups (30.6% gap). The open market for 28 mm induction-wad caps sits at ₹0.85–0.95/pc typical, with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume — so ₹0.81 is well inside what's fair.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 45 days to 30 days after receipt.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Frees ₹16.02 L cash for us. They already take 39d to pay their own suppliers — longer than similar firms at 23d — so asking them to give us 30 days is only fair.

brief.financialLeverage: Cincorp is small (₹4.11 Cr revenue) and we are huge to them — our ₹1.95 Cr spend is 47.43% of everything they sell. They keep about ₹6 of every ₹100 they sell (6.0%), much less than similar firms (15.0%), so price cuts hurt them more than most. They owe 1.13x their own cash and are in the grey zone (Altman Z 1.83), meaning supply is a real watch-out. Push hard on matching our best prices and shortening payment, but keep the relationship stable — losing half their revenue would tip them over, and we need the supply steady.

evidence.point: We pay ₹28.69 L per year more than the lowest prices we already get from other suppliers for the same sort of items.
On PP caps alone, we pay Cincorp ₹1.08/NOS but Mars Plastics charges us ₹0.81/NOS — a 33.2% gap costing us ₹14.05 L a year.
Our ₹1.95 Cr annual spend is 47.43% of their ₹4.11 Cr revenue — we are nearly half their business.
They keep 6.0% profit, well below the 15.0% that similar firms keep.
They take 39d to pay their own suppliers, longer than similar firms at 23d.
Moving to 30-day payment frees ₹16.02 L cash for us.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms. Top second-source candidate with scale and stability.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹1010.97 Cr revenue, health B 73/100) making pails, containers, pharma packaging — a robust, profitable alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd
alternates.why: Listed moulded and blow-moulded packaging firm (₹701.17 Cr revenue, health C 51/100) with broad capability across bottles and caps.

risks: They are in the grey zone (Altman Z 1.83) and burning cash (₹-79.14 L free cash flow) — a small but real supply risk. Don't squeeze so hard that they can't deliver.
We are 47.43% of their revenue. If they lose us, they may not survive. Use that power, but keep the relationship workable — we need the parts.

They keep only 6.0% profit vs 15.0% for similar firms, so price cuts hurt them more. Lead with payment terms (which cost them less) and hold firm on matching our best prices, but don't push for a cut below what we already pay others.
Small entity (₹4.11 Cr) — verify their production capacity and quality systems can handle our volume before relying on them alone. Line up Manjushree or Mold-Tek as a qualified second source.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, but we're paying ₹28.69 lakh more than we do with Mars and Premier for the same items — let's close that gap and tighten payment to 30 days so we both get more predictable.
